correctness.rationale: The stationary covariance is sigma²/(2a)*(I+tL)^(-1). For edges uv, the cofactor expansion on a tree gives q_uv=t B_uv/det K with B_uv=det K[V\{u,v}], while q_vv=A_v/det K, hence rho_uv²=t²B_uv²/(A_u A_v). Principal-minor forests enumerate exact positive polynomial coefficients by marking at most two vertices; positivity ensures squared comparison has same sign as Pearson comparison. Independently generated all nonisomorphic trees n=2..8 using NetworkX, computed exact SymPy determinants of K minors (independent from packaged forest-polynomial verifier), and counted 733 edge pairs across 47 representatives: 201 identically equal, 521 uniformly ordered, eleven with exactly one positive root, in six eight-vertex tree classes. SymPy exact factorizations/Sturm positive-root counts and direct rational check matched the six claimed crossing factor families. For E={01,12,05,23,24,56,57}, direct minor calculation yields a positive prefactor times (t²-4t-1) for rho_12²-rho_01², so t=2+sqrt(5) is unique positive rank reversal. Exhaustion is limited to n<=8 and derives its completeness from the independent graph isomorphism generator, not a sample of trees.

value.rationale: A sharp first topology/size threshold for rank reversals of adjacent stochastic population synchrony is a natural structural question. The classification identifies exactly which small unweighted dispersal networks exhibit nonmonotone *relative* local correlation under changing coupling, with a closed algebraic witness and exhaustive small-tree census. The exact threshold and six exceptional shapes are useful mathematical data beyond known kernel formulas.

final_claim: For stationary homogeneous independently forced OU on a finite simple unweighted tree T, the ordering of adjacent-edge Pearson correlations cannot strictly reverse under positive common dispersal parameter t for |V|<=7; exactly six of the 23 nonisomorphic 8-vertex trees admit reversal, with eleven reversing edge pairs across representatives and exactly one positive crossing per pair; explicit adjacent-edge witness crosses at t=2+sqrt(5).
limitations: Trees of 2..8 vertices only for complete classification; no claims for 9+ or weighted/cyclic graphs.
Exact OU stationary setting has constant a,d,sigma and independent equal-strength noise; changes in ecological models may invalidate threshold.
